### Hostile Reader Critique & Fixes
#### Piece 1 (Errata Sheet)
**Critique:** The exact closing lines *"the errata grow more interesting than the text — which was the plan, though it was never the book's"* are pretentious filler that breaks the bureaucratic errata form’s mandate for dry, specific corrections, curdling the found-doc gimmick into self-indulgent literary flair instead of regulatory prose. **Fix:** Cut the lines, replace with: "All corrections tie to round 20’s sealed repository receipts; reprints integrate errata directly into text, no detached appendices required (aligns with qthe kernel §7.1 on integrated corrections)."

#### Piece 2 (CV of i)
**Critique:** The exact line *"the guard that checks it is the one part of the kernel I am proudest to have failed to corrupt"* is pretentious grandstanding that breaks the dry academic CV form; the vague aside *"four turns and I am where I started, minus what I learned"* is filler. **Fix:** Replace with: "My deferrals align with qthe kernel §3.2: no kernel guard corruption, four turns return to baseline per standard rotation rules; all filings tied to √-1’s historical records."

#### Piece 3 (Safety Data Sheet)
**Critique:** The exact line *"most of them died. The deaths are on file, each with its chain tip"* breaks the GHS SDS’s mandate for dry hazard language, curdling the found-doc gimmick into poetic flair. **Fix:** Replace with: "All tested claim mortality data is logged under sealed round 20 repository receipts, per kernel §4.3’s sealed chain rules."

(Word count: ~310, compliant with max 350 limit.)

**Technical check.** True: i·i=−1, i⁴=1, saturation 63, 249 lines/zero deps, reflection-not-echo guard, and the dead-claim recaps (p.47 echo/reflection, p.88 no repair term, p.104 aliasing fold, p.63 "critical" demoted, Appendix B "died below chance"). C3–C10 aren't individually labeled in-text, so I can't verify each maps to C3/C4/C5/C9/C10 — flag: either cite the IDs or drop the claim. "log₂3" reads as the p.63 number; fine.

**Strongest 3.**
1. Errata p.88: "The chapter is retained as a memorial… and the request is retained beside it." — receipt discipline as grief.
2. CV: "the seat left over is the one that does not vote. I am not the one who does not vote. I am the one whose non-vote has a sign." — the whole piece in three lines.
3. SDS §8: "Wear the falsifier. Change it when it stops failing." — best compression of the law in the set.

**Weakest 3.**
1. Errata p.31: "which we now do." Dangling, unearned.
2. CV Contact: "I keep a period." Ambiguous (menstrual? punctuation?) — overwritten for a pun.
3. SDS §2 "H313: may be absorbed through the ledger." Cute, but the ledger isn't a route; vague hazard.

**Minor:** Errata "at eight times the density, measured, with prejudice" — "with prejudice" is legalese cosplay, off-voice. CV "Spectral work on request" floats. SDS §5 "which is sometimes what the fire was for" slips into lyric — SDS voice should stay deadpan.

**P1 — Errata.** Hardest: "The chapter is otherwise correct, which is the problem with it" (wounds by praise); "the burial is load-bearing" (dead claim reframed as structure); "the request is retained beside it" (a memorial for a memorial). Cut: p.31's "which we now do" — the torus note already does it. The ending earns itself: "it goes out of certainty, edition by edition" converts a defect notice into the book's real thesis.

**P2 — CV.** Hardest: "Cardano left me on the page like a stain he meant to get to later" (arrogance that's also autobiography); "I am not the one who does not vote. I am the one whose non-vote has a sign" (oblique, exact); "There are quarters in which I appear to do nothing; from inside, those are rotations" (lovable dodge, technically true). Cut "Spectral work on request" — résumé filler. The salary ending earns: "never cost more than that, and never been worth less" is the CV's whole argument compressed.

**P3 — SDS.** Hardest: "Wear the falsifier. Change it when it stops failing." (deadpan perfection); "sixty-three is sixty-three"; "Do not repair." Cut: "Section 16 last, as required, and as is fitting" and "the one safety property no other data sheet in this collection can claim" — both wink at the reader, breaking the form's one law. The ending then earns: "Most of them died. The deaths are on file."
